fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to an advisory "Council" and to "recommendations to the" Secretary signal outside-party participation. But this section only makes technical and conforming amendments: it corrects a council's name, redesignates a section, fixes cross-references, and substitutes "Secretary" for "Surgeon General". It does not create or require any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government.
fable.s: by striking out “Council on Alcoholic Abuse” and inserting in lieu thereof “Council on Alcohol Abuse”

opus.w: The section only makes technical fixes: it corrects names, renumbers sections, updates cross-references, and replaces "Surgeon General" with "Secretary". It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. A council is mentioned and recommendations are referenced, but only as wording being corrected, not as a new or changed outside-party role in a federal decision.
opus.s: The second sentence of subsection (a) of section 217 of such Act is amended by striking out “Council on Alcoholic Abuse” and inserting in lieu thereof “Council on Alcohol Abuse”.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section names a "Council on Alcohol Abuse" and amends Section 383 by inserting "Secretary" after "recommendations to the". That language could suggest an advisory body giving input to a federal decision-maker. **Why it fails:** Every change here is a technical, conforming amendment. It fixes a council's name, renumbers a section, changes cross-references, and replaces "Surgeon General" with "Secretary". None of these changes creates, requires, or changes any process where outside parties are consulted before a federal decision. A word like "Council" or "recommendations" showing up in an amendment is not enough.
